I didn’t just play this game—I lived inside it 🤍🌍. The world feels fragile yet warm, platforming flows like a quiet conversation 🎮✨, and every cinematic lands without a single wasted moment 🎥. But the music… 🎶 it doesn’t accompany the journey, it becomes the emotion. Few games understand silence and sound this beautifully 💫.

Playing both parts felt like growing with the story 🌱. The ending left a real emotional weight I still carry 💔, yet even in 2026, this game feels like pure magic ✨. I’m hoping with all my heart for a third part 🙏. My friends—please play both. You’ll feel it ❤️🎮.

To begin this review, I first must say that I have never played a 2D platformer game before. It just isn't my style of game. But after playing OatWotW, I may have changed my view on this genre entirely. I must say, I wouldn't even bat an eye on this game if it didn't have such good reviews and wasn't recommended to me.

Ori has a great and emotional story, I was very immersed and thoroughly enjoyed the whole game. The art style is beautiful, there are many locations, each featuring a different vibe, different enemies and always bringing something new to the gameplay, so you never get bored of repetitiveness. It really does make sense why it has so many good reviews.

I am very glad I listened and had the chance to play and experience this masterpiece.
Very great game! 10/10 in every single aspect!
the gameplay is more complex than Ori and The Blind Forest, but doesnt change its awesomeness, the rest is still beautiful as the first one

One of the best metroidvania-ish games I've ever played. Whether you are in it for the gameplay, the story, the artwork or the music, this game along with its prequel is a must have for every gaming enthusiast. ♪(^∇^*)

Absolutely amazing sequel. Huge improvements on lore, actual sidequests, level design and atmosphere. The blind forest already felt great, but this game easily shits on it's predecessor. 10/10 Metroidvania

Actual 10/10. I'm grasping to find a single flaw with this game. This is up there with Hollow Knight for best metroidvania of recent times. Astonishing work.

The industry needs more games like these instead of 70€ uninished, buggy, microtransaction ridden trash.

Great game.
Everything great about the first Ori game was taken into this one. Will of the Wisps felt more balanced overall with some new mechanics to play with. As usual, beautiful music and a good story.
Amazing game! The story is heartbreaking, the music pulls you in and the gameplay is fun, yet challenging!

This game is an absolute treasure. If you liked the original, you'll love this one - it's the same premise, but with a much higher budget, a lot more polish, and of course, plenty of gut-punches straight to the feels.

It's also a really interesting Metroidvania with a lot of cool and unique skills that have a really "acrobatic" feel. Difficulty-wise, the game can be surprisingly challenging if you want it to be (i.e. selecting the highest difficulty, using shards that increase damage you take, etc.). It can also be pretty easy if you want it to be, too, so don't let the difficulty dissuade you. The world is beautiful and artistic and is a huge draw for me.

In summary: Highly, HIGHLY recommended, but if you haven't played the original, I'd suggest doing that first.

Amazing first improvement to the first game, I love that the game encourages more building of your skills and finding new ones makes you want to consider a slightly different playstyle with each new skill or ability. Plus the sound track as always is the best, love every song that fits so well.

9.5/10. Fantastic sequel to the original that vastly expands core gameplay mechanics and closes the story plot with a serviceable ending. Highlights for me were its epic boss fights, wide cast of characters with their side quests, and an amazing variety of platform puzzles in each biome that kept things fresh from start to end. The world in this instalment felt a lot more lively compared to the first, thanks to the NPCs scattered throughout the game. Loadout customisation is a lot more extensive as there are even more skills and perks to mix and match to your heart's content. No-brainer recommendation if you liked Ori and the Blind Forest.

nice, family friendly game that can be played casually and fixes many of the shortcomings of the previous title.

there are still some sequence breaks (where you stray from the "main path" and intentionally clear hard obstacles with incomplete abilities) i encountered that led to dead ends with no rewards which was always a little disappointing. would be nice to somehow acknowledge the player reaching parts of the game before they were supposed to. (item/experience rewards, achievement, or secret npc encounters with special dialog lines, etc)

After finishing the first game I couldn't wait for this one. The first game was a masterpiece and this one was even better. The music is charming, the graphics are just beautiful and pleasing and the gameplay ties it all up to one of the most brilliant games I've ever played. Oh and the story, prepare yourself for a roller-coaster of emotions, this game can be and is really heartbreaking. Now I feel kinda sad, that this probably is the end of Ori. I love that little creature.

Yeah, sometimes it can be a bit too hard, especially when it comes to boss levels, but once you master the controls, there's nothing more rewarding.

I would highly recommend this game, but please, finish the Blind Forest first for your own good.

The first game was great, so was this one.

I strongly recommend playing it! It may even tug at your heart strings if you are not made of stone.
The visuals are a little overwhelming this time and some stuff blends into the background a little too much, but the style and art direction are absolutely stunning.
The audio contributes a lot to building the atmosphere of the game.
It may be more challenging than one may expect initially. In the first game I was quite amazed how much stuff one can still get out of a 2d metroidvania platformer...and they did it again. The skills are interesting and bring a lot of variation.

A gem of a game that should be on everyone's list!
This game is just so incredible. Like its predecessor, its music, design, and emotional story are so catching. I love this game.

A stunning sequel to "Ori and the Blind Forest".
Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a beautifully crafted game and wonderful to experience, and I would definitely recommend it to anyone.

This game has such gorgeous art, music, aesthetics and the platforming is very light, airy and fun. My only problem with the game so far is that it is very laggy. My screen often freezes and the only way to get out of it is to exit the game and restart it, and I've encountered a few other glitches like little life giving buds not respawning, necessary blue lanterns not being there in the Watermill chase and such. But if a little lag is my only complaint about the game then I think the game is doing a pretty good job. I highly recommend!

Edit: I have now beaten the game and my opinion still stands :)) ! The only problem I really have with the game is how much it lags on my computer which I bought only 6 months ago. It got a bit annoying when I was in the later stages of boss battles or escape sequences and it lagged so badly I had to exit the game since it doesn't save progress within a challenge. The art is beautiful, the music has been playing on repeat in my head and I absolutely adore the story and its ending. 10/10 would play again

One of the best platformers I've ever played. They took everything that was great about the original and made it even better, with truly amazing gameplay especially with the jump/glide/bash/dash/launch combinations that are just next level. My only criticism is there are too many skills that are not useful, like the attacking orb and the boomerang star (and flap is terrible too but necessary for various points in the game). But once you get your loadout dialed in and settle into your style of play, you are going to love conquering this beautiful world and its cute-but-deadly creatures. 

I really can't say enough about this game. A beautiful story, ultra creative design, and rewarding gameplay that brought back my love for controllers. It is worth far, far more than its asking price, and will leave you devastated once it's over.

**Ori and the Will of the Wisps** is a visually stunning action-adventure platformer developed by Moon Studios. Released in 2020, it's the sequel to **Ori and the Blind Forest** and continues the story of Ori, a small guardian spirit.

The game features a beautifully crafted hand-drawn world, rich with vibrant colors and emotional storytelling. Players navigate through expansive environments filled with puzzles, challenging platforming segments, and combat against various enemies. The gameplay introduces new abilities and mechanics, allowing for more fluid movement and exploration.

A standout aspect of **Will of the Wisps** is its emotional narrative, exploring themes of love, loss, and friendship. The game also features a captivating musical score that enhances the overall experience. It's widely praised for its art style, gameplay mechanics, and heartfelt story. Did you enjoy the first game, or do you have a favorite moment from the sequel?

Absolutely amazing. I usually find video game sequels to be worse than the first game, but Moon Studios found a way to do otherwise. The game's graphics and artstyle are beautiful, the story is charming, and the new features such as new moves, new abilities, and others are a really nice addition to the sequel. The secrets are fun to find as always, and the game is just... fun! It feels good to control Ori (except when swimming), and the side quests are also a nice addition. The only problems I have with the game are the autosave feature, the HUGE difficulty spikes, and... the ending. I understand that they wanted to end the Ori series so they could work on new games, but that ending REALLY made me think of Darling in the Franxx. Anyway, I strongly recommend picking this game up if you like metroidvainas, and I'm sure you'll have a lot of fun with it. I did. Good job, Moon Studios.

Easily up there with the greatest. The first game was already beautiful, and this one is even more so. I loved the first game, but it felt very punishing at times. Will of the Wisps fixes every issue I had with the first game, namely the frustratingly punishing difficulty and the combat, and expands on the game to make it a true masterpiece. Exploring is super fun, the movement is some of my favorite in gaming, and the combat is actually super enjoyable now! Honestly can't think of a single thing I disliked about the game, but a bajillion things I loved about it. Easy 10/10
Very nice game, I love the combat. I'm not really that interested in the story but i like some of the characters.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (97%): players love the graphics and the story, and the combat draws the most complaints.
Bugs and crashes are the next most common complaint.

details.text: Players who are just starting out are much less positive (80%) than those who have put in many hours (98%).
Combat complaints have ticked up in recent reviews, so buyers who dislike combat should weigh that.
